topic: Acute Agitation & Aggression - De-escalation & Pharmacological Management
improvements_verified: ✅ De-escalation techniques FIRST-LINE: Calm tone, empathy, active listening, clear language, offer choices, set limits
✅ Environmental modifications: Remove audience, reduce stimulation, remove weapons, exit route, staff safety
✅ Pharmacological sedation: Offer ORAL first (olanzapine 5-10mg, lorazepam 1-2mg), then IM if refuses
✅ IM options: Olanzapine 5-10mg IM (onset 15-30min) OR haloperidol 5mg + promethazine 25-50mg IM OR midazolam 5-10mg IM
✅ CRITICAL SAFETY: DO NOT combine IM olanzapine + IM benzodiazepine (respiratory depression risk)
✅ Droperidol 5-10mg IM: QT prolongation risk, ECG pre/post required
✅ Physical restraint LAST RESORT: Minimum force, document time/reason/staff/injuries, vital signs q15min, medical review <15min
✅ Monitoring: Vitals q15min x1h then hourly, respiratory rate (sedation), ECG if droperidol, EPS (dystonia, akathisia)
✅ Complications: NMS (fever, rigidity, ↑CK), dystonia (benztropine 1-2mg IM), QT prolongation (avoid droperidol if QTc >500ms)
✅ Australian doses (NOT US doses - US often uses haloperidol 10mg, we use 5mg)
✅ SAFE-T for underlying condition: Agitation may be from psychosis with suicidal ideation
remaining_issues: ⚠️ Cultural safety: De-escalation techniques may differ for Aboriginal/TSI patients (trauma-informed care not emphasized)
⚠️ No mention of interpreter services for CALD patients in acute agitation
comparison_to_previous: Previous: ~5.8/10 (medication safety issues, no de-escalation emphasis) → Current: 9.4/10 (COMPREHENSIVE) - +62% improvement

improvements_verified: ✅ SAFE-T assessment: Psychosis = high suicide risk (15% lifetime risk in schizophrenia), assess for command hallucinations
✅ Differential diagnosis: Primary psychotic disorders, substance-induced (ICE, cannabis, LSD), medical causes (encephalitis, stroke, thyrotoxicosis), delirium (medical emergency)
✅ Initial assessment: Safety (self-harm, aggression), medical clearance (obs, BSL, UEC, TFTs, urine drug screen, CT head if indicated), collateral history, MSE, capacity
✅ Behavioral management FIRST: De-escalation, calm environment, reduce stimulation, verbal engagement, space, security
✅ Oral medication preferred: Olanzapine 5-10mg, risperidone 1-2mg, quetiapine 50-100mg, PLUS lorazepam 1-2mg, wait 30-60min before repeating
✅ IM medication: Olanzapine 5-10mg IM (DO NOT combine with IM benzo) OR haloperidol 5mg + promethazine 25-50mg OR midazolam 5-10mg OR droperidol 5-10mg (QT risk)
✅ Physical restraint: Last resort, minimum force, document, medical review <15min
✅ Monitoring: Vitals q15min x1h then hourly, respiratory rate, ECG if droperidol, EPS monitoring
✅ Complications: NMS (fever, rigidity, autonomic instability, ↑CK), dystonia (oculogyric crisis, benztropine 1-2mg IM), QT prolongation (avoid droperidol if QTc >500ms)
✅ Australian medication doses and protocols
remaining_issues: ⚠️ Cultural interpretation of psychosis: Aboriginal/TSI cultural/spiritual experiences vs pathological psychosis (not mentioned)
⚠️ Substance-induced psychosis: Methamphetamine ('ICE') epidemic in Australia, particularly rural/regional areas (could emphasize)
⚠️ No mention of family involvement in culturally appropriate way
